full_judgment:
4. The Respondent filed affidavit-in-opposition sworn by the Asstt. Director (Local Govt.) Rangpur controverting the allegations and statements made in the petition. It is asserted that the suspension order as issued by the Secretary Ministry of Local Govt. is quite in accordance with the statutory provision of law. It is also strongly denied that there has been misuse of power or violation of law on the part of Govt. in passing the order of suspension. It is further stated that there are allegations of corruption, misappropriation of Govt. money and misuse of official power against the petitioner for which the impugned order was issued on the basis of said allegations and pending the completion of enquiry the petitioner has rightly been placed under suspension to check further misappropriation and misuse of power by him. It is also stated that the petitioner has filed suit being suit. No. 18(87 and Misc. Case No. 11 of 1987 in the Civil Court against the District Magistrate, Rangpur. 

 5. Affidavit-in-reply was also filed on behalf of the petitioner controverting the statements and averment made in the affidavit-in-opposition asserting that the suspension order in question was issued by way of misusing the power by the prescribed authority in violation of statutory provision of law and has offended the principle of natural justice. The respondent thereafter filed supplementary affidavit stating that upon a complaint filed by District Anti-Corruption Officer, Rangpur a criminal case was started against the petitioner being C.R. Case No. 160/87 dated 30.6.85 in the court of Upazila Magistrate Mithapukur, District Rangpur. The petition filed by the District Anti-Corruption Officer, Rangpur has been annexed with the supplementary affidavit filed on behalf of the Respondent but no copy of the order sheet from any court has been filed to show whether any criminal proceeding has been started or pending against the petitioner. The petitioner has also controverted the statements and allegations made in the supplementary affidavit stating that the allegations are false and he has became a victim to the conspiracy as he made several complaints to different authorities against the corrupt practices of the Deputy Commissioner and the District Ad-ministration, Rangpur. 

 9. Mr. Kaiseruddin Ahmed, the learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing for the Respondent, straight away admits that no proceeding under section 13 of the Ordinance has been started for the removal of the petitioner from the office of Chairman of Mithapukur Upazila Parishad but he denies the petitioner's contention that charge of misuse of power, corruption and misconduct is unfounded and petitioner has been victimised without holding any enquiry which is an essential prerequisite under the statute. The learned Deputy Attorney-General submits that there are allegations of corruption and misappropriation of money against the petitioner for which enquiry has started according to the provision of law and the impugned order was made on the basis of multifarious allegations received from different quarters and, therefore, he has rightly been placed under suspension till the completion of the enquiry. The learned Deputy Attorney-General further submits that initiation of Criminal proceeding against the petitioner consequent on the complaint filed by the District Anti-Corruption Officer, Rangpur in the court of Upazila Magistrate, are sufficient grounds for placing the petitioner under suspension and in that view of the matter the order of suspension can not be called in question as being violative of the statute. 

 10. Section 13 of the Local Government (Thana Parishad and Thana Administration) (Reorganisation) Ordinance, 1982 (Ordinance No. LIX of 1982) provides grounds as well as the procedure for the removal of a Chairman from his office as Upazila Chairman. In the present case the question of removal is not the relevant point for decision and hence it is not necessary for us to enter into discussion of the same. The question mooted before us is the order of suspension of Chairman from his office. So for the purpose of determining the validity or otherwise of the order of suspension it will be necessary and proper for us to examine the law relating to suspension which has been provided in section 13(A) by way of amendment of Local Govt. (Thana Parishad and Thana Administration Reorganisation) Ordinance 1982 on 4.6.87 called as The Local Govt. (Upazila Parishad and Upazila Administration Reorganisation (Amendment) Ordinance 1987 which reads as:- 

 "13A suspension of Chairman (1) where any proceeding has been initiated for removal of a Chairman under section 13, or where any Criminal proceeding under any law have been started against the Chairman, or where on an enquiry made by the Government, he is found to be guilty of misconduct within the meaning of section 13(1) or is found to be involved in the activities detrimental to the interest of the Parishad and in the opinion of the Govt. the exercise of powers by him as Chairman is either likely to be prejudicial to the interest of the parishad or undesirable from point of view of public interest, the Govt. may by order in writing, place such Chairman under suspension". 

 (3) When on an enquiry made by the Govt. he is found to be guilty of misconduct, or (b) he is found to be involved in activities adverse to the interest of the Parishad and in the opinion of the Govt. the exercise of the powers by him as Chairman is either likely to be prejudicial to the interest of the Parishad or undesirable from the point of view of public interest. Now let us go through the contents of the impugned order of suspension made against the petitioner by the authority on 17.10.87 (Annexure 'A') which is reproduced below: 

 13. The second point which could be taken as a ground for suspending a Chairman from his office by the prescribed authority, according to the provision of the Ordinance, is the pendency of Criminal Proceedings, if there be any, against the petitioner. The learned Deputy Attorney-General submits that Criminal Proceedings arc pending against the petitioner and those proceedings have given rise to the occasion for the authority to make an order of suspension against him. In support of his submission he has referred to the petition of complaint filed by the District Anti-corruption Officer which has been annexed with the supplementary affidavit. Besides the petition of complaint, the learned Advocate could not produce any order of the court or any other material to show that cognizance of any criminal offence has been taken or criminal case has been started in any court against the petitioner and that criminal proceeding is now pending. According to the provision laid down in section 13(A)(1) of the Ordinance a Chairman can also be placed under suspension if found to be guilty of misconduct within the meaning of section 13(1) of the Ordinance or if he is found to have been involved in the activities detrimental to the interest of the Parishad in the opinion of the Govt. and exercise of the power by the Chairman is either likely to prejudice the interest of the Parishad or undesirable from the point of view of public interest. Now the question is what will be the criteria for forming such opinion and for arriving at such a finding which will enable the prescribed authority to make an order of suspension of the Chairman from his office. The answer to the question is available from the reading of section 13(A) of the Ordinance which provides for holding an enquiry which is made an assential prerequisite of forming opinion so as to place the Chairman under suspension. According to the scheme for constitution of Local Govt. Institution, powers are given to the Local Parishad for functioning but under the ultimate supervision of the Prescribed Authority, who is the head of the Local Administration. Chairman is elected by the people of the area and he is to function until he loses the confidence of the members of the Parishad or be re-moved under the provision of the Ordinance. The above principle has been clearly laid down by the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court in the case reported in 1981 BLD (AD) 196. 

 15. The learned Deputy Attorney-General concedes to the point of law and candidly admits that holding of enquiry has been made an assential requirements of law before forming an opinion by the authority against an elected representative like the Chairman of the Parishad for making the order of suspension. The very order of suspension presupposes that there had been enquiry in the matter, the learned Deputy Attorney-General submits, but when called upon he could not produce any material from the record to 'show that such enquiry has been held in the present case and the enquiry report has been made the basis of formation of opinion of the prescribed authority before placing the petitioner under suspension. 

 16. The learned Advocate for the petitioner has referred to the case of Abdul Rye Bhuiya Vs. Secretary, Ministry of Local Govt. and Rural Development arid others reported in 1981 BLD( AD) 196 wherein similar question was raised regarding the application of mind of the authority to the criminal proceedings pending against the Chairman and the following principle has been laid down: 

 17. In the case under reference a Criminal Proceeding was found to have been started against the Chairman for which he was placed under suspension but the order was declared not sustainable in law as there was no application of mind of the authority to the Criminal Proceeding or its effect on the exercise of power by the Chairman or forming of any opinion on it. 

 18. In the present case the Criminal Proceeding though spoken of has not been taken as a ground in the order, the petitioner has been suspended on some other grounds in respect of which also holding of enquiry and formation of opinion on any of the grounds taken in the impugned order are essential prerequisites which appears to have not been followed by the authority before making the order of suspension. 

 19. The next point urged by the learned Advocate for the petitioner is that before passing the order placing the petitioner under suspension no notice was served upon him giving him the opportunity to explain his position in respect of the allegations made against him and thus there has been violation of principle of natural justice. As against this submission of the learned Advocate' for the petitioner, the learned Deputy Attorney-General submits that the principle of natural justice cannot be invoked in all cases particularly in a case like the present one where the point at issue is not removal but suspension which is merely temporary deprivition of petitioner's right to hold office pending enquiry. We are unable to accept the argument of the learned Deputy Attorney-General as we find that the rule of natural justice is an indispensable rule of practice, whenever any decision is made directly affecting a person's right to property or character of office, the rule is to be read in every enactment, even though there is no positive word to that effect, provided that there is no specific prohibition to the contrary. The above principle has been laid down in a series of decisions of the superior court of the country and also in the case of Abdur Rashid Versus Govt. of Bangladesh reported in 32 DLR page 109.
